points: A live example, not slides. This is the idea system in this repository, walked end to end. The point: what a skill is, versus a command, a subagent and a tool — and why one decision stays behind a command only the owner types.

/orient — what this agent can do here, right now. Every command, skill and tool listed below is read from disk at run time, not from a stored list. An empty category is reported as empty, not guessed.

/idea — recording an idea through the sanctioned writer. This command hands the idea to tools/append_idea.py, which assigns an id and validates the entry. The idea log is append-only: no line in it is ever edited or deleted.

/idea-triage — a subagent reads the idea and reports. The command hands the idea to a subagent, which finds related plans and documents and writes one finding. It can move the idea to triaged and no further — that limit is deliberate.

Plan beat — from idea to governed work. The idea just recorded becomes a requirement, a plan and backlog phases: the same hand-off every piece of work in this repository goes through. No command runs during this step.

Overview-skill rebuild — one script, run, reported. The d-system-overview skill calls tools/generate_overview.py and reports exactly what it printed. It never recomputes a number itself; the tools own every figure on the page.

Test — the same page, updated with real data. The regenerated overview now shows the idea just recorded, not a placeholder. The terminal and the talking-points panel keep working through the same run.

Four different things, one protected boundary. A skill, a command, a subagent and a tool each do a different job here. /session-close is the one decision that stays behind a command a person types — no agent can reach it.
